title: DP IV: Bitmask DP (Subset / TSP / Assignment) & Digit DP
relevance: Medium (harder OAs reuse assignment-under-mask and "count numbers in [L,R] with a digit property"; essential for CF ~1600–2100, not as common as knapsack/LCS in easy screens)
company_notes: Assign n workers to n jobs with a compatibility matrix (count ways / max score) → Matching / assignment bitmask. Minimum trips / days / buses under capacity W → Elevator Rides subset packing. Count integers in [L,R] with a digit property (digit-sum divisible by k / at most 3 non-zero digits / no equal adjacent digits) → Digit DP. Order n≤20 tasks with pairwise adjacency bonuses → TSP-style dp[mask][last].

phases.goal: Confirm the candidate spots bitmask DP versus digit DP from constraints and wording.

must_hit.point: Spot bitmask DP when n≤20 or the ask is to assign / visit / choose a subset of roles.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names n≤20 or assign/visit/subset-of-roles as the bitmask trigger.

must_hit.point: Spot digit DP when the range is up to 10^18 (or a huge digit string) and the constraint is on digits.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Ties a huge numeric bound plus a digit property to digit DP instead of looping the range.

must_hit.point: OA flavors: worker–job assignment, capacity packing under W, count in [L,R] with a digit property, or visit-all order with pairwise bonuses.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps at least one of those phrasings to Matching, Elevator Rides, Digit DP, or TSP-style mask DP.

probes: Is this bitmask DP or digit DP—and which constraint or phrase tipped you off?

hints.1: Look at how large n is, and whether the ask is about digits of a numeric range.
hints.2: Small n with assign/visit/subset → bitmask; huge [L,R] with a digit rule → digit DP.
hints.3: n≤20 or assign/visit/roles → bitmask; range up to 10^18 (or a huge digit string) with a digit constraint → digit DP.

phases.goal: Lock the state shape: mask, mask+end, assignment by unused bit, or digit DFS with tight.

must_hit.point: Typical bitmask states: dp[mask] best over subset mask; dp[mask][i] best path visiting mask ending at i (TSP / Hamiltonian); or dp[mask] ways to assign the next free person to an unused bit.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names at least one of those three state shapes and what the mask (and optional end index) means.

must_hit.point: Digit DP builds numbers left-to-right against an upper bound with state (pos, tight, started, extra); answer [L,R] as f(R)-f(L-1).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions tight/started/extra and subtracting the (L-1) upper-bound solve for a range.

must_hit.point: Transitions flip one bit, or enumerate submasks; digit extra tracks digit-sum / remainder / nonzero-count / last digit / used-digit mask.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes bit-flip or submask moves, or what extra carries for the digit constraint.

probes: What is your DP state—dp[mask], dp[mask][i], or digit (pos, tight, …)—and how do you answer a range [L,R]?

hints.1: Ask whether you encode a small set of items/cities/roles or walk digits of an upper bound.
hints.2: Subset/path/assignment → mask states; digit property on a bound → (pos, tight, started, extra).
hints.3: Use dp[mask] / dp[mask][i] / assignment to an unused bit; for digits, dfs with tight and answer f(R)-f(L-1).

phases.goal: Verify templates for assignment, TSP, elevator packing, submasks, and digit DFS.

must_hit.point: Assignment template: dp[0]=1; for each mask, let i=__builtin_popcount(mask), try unmatched j compatible with person i.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sketches popcount-as-person-index and trying unused partners starting from dp[0]=1.

must_hit.point: TSP / Hamiltonian: dp[1<<s][s]=1 (or 0 cost); transition dp[mask][v] → dp[mask|(1<<u)][u] over edges v→u.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Writes the single-source seed and the extend-by-unused-neighbor transition.

must_hit.point: Elevator / subset packing stores (min_rides, load_in_last_ride) per mask; digit DFS uses limit = tight ? digits[pos] : 9 with memo.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions the rides/load pair and/or looping digits up to the tight limit of 9.

must_hit.point: Submask enumeration: for (int sub=mask; sub; sub=(sub-1)&mask).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Writes the (sub-1)&mask loop over nonempty submasks.

probes: Code the assignment or TSP transition from a mask, then sketch digit DFS with the tight digit limit.

hints.1: Start from the empty mask or a single starting city, then extend by one unused bit.
hints.2: Assignment uses popcount as the next person; TSP extends with mask|(1<<u); digit loops 0..limit.
hints.3: dp[0]=1 with popcount person i; dp[1<<s][s] then mask|(1<<u); elevator (rides, last_load); digit limit = tight ? digits[pos] : 9; submasks via (sub-1)&mask.

phases.goal: Anchor when bitmask fits, when digit DP is required, and the submask O(3^n) cost.

must_hit.point: Use bitmask DP when n≤20; use digit DP when R≤10^18 (or a huge digit string) with a digit property.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States those two constraint cutovers without inventing a time bound not in the source.
Quotes O(3^n) for the submask DP pattern (Grouping-style).

probes: When do you reach for bitmask versus digit DP, and what is the cost of enumerating all submasks?

hints.1: Compare n to the subset-encoding limit, and the numeric bound to something you cannot loop.
hints.2: n≤20 → mask; R≤10^18 plus a digit rule → digit DP; partitioning via submasks has a named exponential.
hints.3: n≤20 bitmask; R≤10^18 digit DP; submask enumeration is O(3^n).

phases.goal: Catch leading-zero bugs, wrong range handling, and missing last-city state.

must_hit.point: Always handle leading zeros with a started flag so previous digit / nonzero count do not treat padding zeros as real digits.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Calls out started/leading-zero so adj≠ or nonzero counts ignore prefix padding.

must_hit.point: Range answers must be solve(R)-solve(L-1), not a single upper-bound call on R alone.
Both techniques combine when digit DP carries a used-digit mask inside the digit state.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions used-digit mask inside digit DP (permutation-of-digits / distinct-digit styles).

probes: What breaks digit DP if you forget leading zeros or answer [L,R] with only f(R)?

hints.1: Think about prefix zeros and how a range [L,R] reduces to upper-bound solves.
hints.2: Padding zeros are not real digits; ranges need two upper-bound solves.
hints.3: Use started so prev/nonzero ignore padding; answer f(R)-f(L-1); used-digit mask can live inside digit DP.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: Use bitmask when n≤20 or the task is assign / visit / choose a subset of roles; use digit DP when the range is up to 10^18 (or a huge digit string) and the constraint is on digits.
dp[mask] is enough for subset best/ways or assignment; dp[mask][i] is needed for TSP / Hamiltonian paths that care where the path ends.
Flip one bit to add an item/city/person; enumerate submasks in O(3^n) when partitioning a set into groups.

tradeoffs.topic: Pure digit DP vs used-digit mask inside digit DP
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Plain digit DP tracks tight/started/extra (digit-sum, remainder, nonzero-count, last digit); when distinct used digits matter, carry a used-digit mask inside the digit state.

gotchas.trap: Treating leading/padding zeros as real digits for previous-digit or nonzero-count constraints.
gotchas.correction: Keep a started flag so padding zeros do not count as digits or set prev.

gotchas.trap: Answering count-in-[L,R] with only an upper-bound solve on R.
gotchas.correction: Compute solve(R)-solve(L-1) (Classy Numbers / Counting Numbers style).

gotchas.trap: Using plain dp[mask] for a visit-all path with pairwise adjacency bonuses that depend on the last city.
gotchas.correction: Use TSP-style dp[mask][last] (Kefa and Dishes / Hamiltonian Flights).

gotchas.trap: Forgetting elevator state needs both ride count and load in the last ride.
gotchas.correction: Store (min_rides, load_in_last_ride) per mask and try adding into the last ride or starting a new one.
